newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian ruler says next leader will be civilian.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian ruler says next leader will be civilian.

text.p: Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha says his government will hand over to an elected civilian president next year, but he has still not made clear if he will stand in the election aimed at restoring democracy.

"I can assure you that this administration will definitely hand over to a democratically elected civilian president next year," Abacha said in a message to an air force officers meeting in the northern city of Kaduna on Monday.
In the message, Abacha did not specifically address the subject of his possible candidacy in elections set for late summer 1998.

But it was the clearest statement so far from the army ruler indicating he was not in support of the growing number of newspaper advertisements calling on him to shed his army uniform and stand as a candidate.

The advertisements are placed by groups that have sprung up in several parts of Nigeria calling on Abacha to stand in the election and continue in power beyond October 1, 1998 -- the date that he has set for a handover to an elected president.
A government statement issued in the capital Abuja on Sunday denounced the lobby, saying it was undermining the transition-to-civil-rule programme.

In the message to the air force officers read by his chief of defence staff, Major-General Abdulsalam Abubakar, Abacha said his government remained totally committed to the transition programme despite lack of support for it from "some sections of the international community."
"Be rest assured that everything humanly possible will be made to ensure that a civilian takes over as the president of this great country in 1998," he said.
Nigeria has been in political turmoil since the army annulled a presidential vote in 1993 presumed to have been won by wealthy businessman Moshood Abiola.

Abacha's transition-to-democracy programme is derided by the opposition as a charade because of the continued detention of Abiola and the non-registration of political parties formed by government opponents.
